declarations.name: runStagesSync
declarations.description:
Run a `sync` pipeline to completion synchronously — for triggers that ride the
browser's native synchronous events (paste / copy / keydown) and cannot await.
Stages must return an outcome directly; an async or interactive stage throws
(the design-doc contract that dialogs/awaits belong only to deferred pipelines).

declarations.name: runStages

type.text: { signal: AbortSignal; ui: InteractionHost; generation: number }

declarations.description:
Run every stage in order, threading the context. The optional `report` observer
sees each stage transition (running → ok/skipped/halted/error/aborted) for
step-level visualization. Throws only on an unexpected stage error (after
reporting it).

The loader threshold of one deferred run. `pending` fires only when actual work
outlasts `thresholdMs`: the clock starts with the run and restarts after each
interactive request settles; while a request is open (a dialog waiting for the
user) the clock is stopped and the run reports `waiting` (which also retracts a
`pending` already shown). Interactive stages must go through `wrap(host)`.
declarations.name: PendingGate

members.name: start
members.description: Start (or restart) the threshold clock.

members.name: stop
members.description: The run settled: no more `pending` / `waiting` from this gate.

members.name: wrap
members.description: `host`, with the clock paused while each of its requests is open.

declarations.description:
Debounced, cancellable runner for a single deferred pipeline. Call `schedule()`
on each change; it coalesces, runs once idle, drops stale results, and only
surfaces `pending` if the run's work outlasts the threshold (`PendingGate`).
declarations.name: DeferredRunner

`preview`) keeps only the view-mode group, so the user can switch back.

members.name: #applyVisibility
members.description: Show the groups that pass the editable filter and have a visible item; dividers only between shown groups; hide an empty zone.

members.name: mount
members.description: The persistent editor surface. The engine mounts its view here, once.

members.name: toolbarMount
members.description: Persistent slot for the static (zone) toolbar.

members.name: statusTopMount
members.description: Persistent slots for the dedicated status bar(s) — top and bottom edges.

members.name: overlayLayer
members.description: Persistent shadow-local layer the floating presenters portal into.

members.name: pendingMount
members.description: Persistent slot for the pipeline pending loader (corner of the editor body; `hidden` when idle).

members.name: setDefaultOutputFormat
members.description: Seed the split output lens (before the user clicks a tab).

members.name: render
members.description:
(Re)build the shadow structure for `mode` + `toolbarSide`. The toolbar slot
and the editor mount are wrapped in one bordered `.we-surface` frame (so the
toolbar sits flush against the editor, with a divider, rather than floating as
a separate card); `toolbarSide` sets which edge the toolbar occupies. Builds
the output panel only for `split`; (re)anchors only for `inline`.

members.name: refreshOutput
members.description: Refresh the split output panel in place (no structural change).

members.name: deactivate
members.description:
Release live positioning resources without tearing down the structure.
The element calls this on `disconnect()` so a detached-but-held `inline`
editor doesn't keep a floating-ui `autoUpdate` loop running against its
detached host; a reconnect re-anchors via `render()`.

members.name: activate
members.description:
Re-acquire live positioning after deactivate (the host was
reconnected): re-anchors an `inline` editor without rebuilding the shadow
structure, so the editor mount — and the live view — stays where it is.

members.name: setInert
members.description: `disabled`: make the whole surface (editor, toolbar, status, output) `inert`.

declarations.name: domRect
declarations.description:
A plain `DOMRect`-shaped object for a core `/positioning` virtual reference.
Built by hand (rather than `new DOMRect`) so it works identically in the
browser and in happy-dom, and so a caller can recompute it per frame (the
selection rect the selection toolbar anchors to).

members.name: formAssociated
members.description: Form-associated for `<fieldset disabled>` (core `isEffectivelyDisabled`) and `el.form`.

members.name: #layout
members.default: new ViewLayout({ shadow: this.#shadow, host: this, serialize: (fmt) => (this.#engine ? this.#engine.serialize(fmt) : ''), })

members.name: #customStyles
members.description: Instance + page-wide custom CSS (core `createCustomStyles`, created on the first build).

members.name: #removeLoader
members.description: Removes the pending loader (core `renderLoader`); set while it shows.

members.name: #hasFormatError
members.description: Whether the host is currently invalid because of a throwing `getValueFormatCallback`.

type.text: { value: string; format: EditorFormat; valueAtSet: unknown } | undefined

members.name: reinit
members.description: Content source changed (or first connect): (re)build the engine.

members.name: #applyCustomStyles
members.description: Custom CSS, the canonical core adoption (core usage.md → "Style injection", rulebook C-CA-15).

members.name: disabledChanged
members.description:
`isDisabled` or an ancestor `<fieldset disabled>` flipped (core merges both
into `isEffectivelyDisabled`): toggle editing, the chrome and `inert`.

members.name: formResetCallback
members.description:
The surrounding `<form>` was reset: restore the initial content (`defaultValue`,
attribute `value`), like a native control — silently: a native `form.reset()`
fires no `input` / `change`, so neither does this (the hidden input is synced).

members.name: update
members.description: Cosmetic/behavioural change: patch the live engine without a rebuild.

members.name: connect
members.description:
Activate (every connect, after any reinit()/update()). Core's build-once
model: the engine survives a DOM move, so this only resumes live resources —
the view's DOM observer, the inline anchor, the chrome's selection state.
Content, selection and undo history are exactly as they were.

members.name: disconnect
members.description:
Deactivate (every disconnect): release live resources only — the engine (and
with it the document, selection and undo history) stays alive, so a DOM move
re-activates without a rebuild and a detached editor still answers `value`.

members.name: #createEngine
members.description: Lay out the shadow and construct an engine from #seed (throws on a bad plugin set).

members.name: #wireEngine
members.description: Adopt a freshly constructed engine: events, chrome, activation state, `ready`.

members.name: #setPendingLoader
members.description:
Show / hide the pipeline pending loader through core `renderLoader()`:
instance `renderLoadingCallback` → page-wide `renderLoadingCallback` →
the default `.we__loader` spinner; `role="status"` + label `loading`.

members.name: #syncFormInput
members.description:
Form convention (KeenMate suite, like web-multiselect): a light-DOM hidden
input named by `name` carries the live content in `contentFormat` — the host
never calls `setFormValue`. No `name` → no input. Disabled (not submitted)
while the editor is effectively disabled.

members.name: #formValue
members.description:
The submitted form value: the document in `contentFormat`, through
`getValueFormatCallback` when set. A throwing callback submits `''`, marks the
host invalid (core `setFormatError`, label `valueFormatError`) and fires
`value-format-error`; the next successful format clears the invalid state.

members.name: #applyLayout
members.description: (Re)arrange the shadow layout for the current view mode + anchor + toolbar + status side.

members.name: #applyChromeState
members.description: Push the current editable + toolbar + status-bar settings into the chrome.

members.name: #applyContentOption
members.description: Map a content string + format onto the matching engine option.

members.name: createController
members.description: The public facade (`el.controller`): content I/O, focus, commands — never the engine.

members.name: #runCommand
members.description: A registered command / pipeline by name, or a ProseMirror command on the live view.

members.name: value
members.description:
The live content, serialized in the active `contentFormat` (`''` before the first
build). Assigning replaces the document, parsed in `contentFormat` — like
`setValue(value, undefined, { isSilent: true })`: silent (no `change`, like a
native `input.value`); the hidden form input is synced. The `value` ATTRIBUTE is the initial content
(defaultValue) and is never written.

members.name: setValue
members.description:
Replace the document with `value`, parsed in `format` (defaults to the active
`contentFormat`) — the controller's write path. Fires `change` unless
`options.isSilent`; assigning `el.value` is the silent form (like a native
`input.value`). Either way the hidden form input is synced.

members.name: setViewMode
members.description:
Switch the view mode (`edit` | `split` | `preview` | `inline`). Fires
`view-mode-change` (`source: 'api'`) unless `options.isSilent`; a no-op (no event)
when `mode` is already active, and an invalid mode warns and keeps the current one.
Assigning `el.viewMode` is the silent form.

members.name: #switchViewMode
members.description: The one view-mode write path behind `setViewMode()`, the view-mode commands and the plugin port.

members.name: plugins
members.description:
The editor plugin set. Assign to customise — compose with `defaultPlugins()`
to keep the built-ins, and order the array to control conflict precedence
(later plugins override earlier by id). Reassigning rebuilds the engine on the
new set, preserving the live content. Reading returns the active set.

```js
import { defaultPlugins } from '@keenmate/web-editor';
el.plugins = [...defaultPlugins(), myPlugin];
```

members.name: destroyCallback
members.description:
Final teardown (core `destroy()` calls this once): the engine — document,
undo history, plugins' `destroy()` — and the shadow layout. `disconnect()`
keeps both alive for a DOM move; this releases them for good.

members.name: defaultValue
members.description: Initial / default content, interpreted per `contentFormat` (like a native input’s `value` attribute ↔ `defaultValue`). Changing it replaces the document. The live content is the `value` PROPERTY.

members.name: contentFormat
members.description: The format of the one document — the lens for content I/O (the `value` attribute and property, the `change` event): 'markdown' (default), 'html', or 'json'. Switching it re-reports the SAME document in the new format — it never rebuilds the document, and (like any assignment) fires no `change`.

members.name: name
members.description: Form field name. When set, a light-DOM `<input type="hidden" name="…">` child of the host carries the live content (serialized in `contentFormat`) and submits with the surrounding `<form>`; it is disabled (not submitted) while the editor is disabled, including by a `<fieldset disabled>`. A form reset restores `defaultValue` (attribute `value`) silently — no `change`, like a native `form.reset()`.

members.name: getValueFormatCallback
members.description: Property only. `(ctx) => string` — formats the value written into the hidden form input (`name`), e.g. to sanitize HTML. `ctx`: `{ value, contentFormat }` (the document in the active `contentFormat`) + `controller` / `element`. Affects ONLY the submitted form value: `el.value` and the `change` detail stay the document in `contentFormat`. Called on every sync of the form input (each change). A throw is logged (error), the hidden input gets an empty string, the host turns invalid (label `valueFormatError`) and `value-format-error` fires; the next successful format clears it.

members.name: viewMode
members.description: Presentation: 'edit' (default), 'split' (editor + live output), 'preview' (read-only render), or 'inline' (overlay chrome on a live-page element). `preview` forces read-only. Full layouts arrive in Phase 3; for now the view mode is stored and reflected. Assigning it (property or attribute) is silent — no `view-mode-change`; `setViewMode()` and the view-mode toolbar items fire it.

members.name: isReadonly
members.description: Read-only: the content can’t change (no typing, toolbar hidden), but it stays focusable, selectable and copyable. `view-mode="preview"` also forces this on. Reflects to `readonly`.

members.name: isDisabled
members.description: Disabled: no interaction at all — not editable, not focusable or selectable (the surface is `inert`), toolbar hidden. An ancestor `<fieldset disabled>` disables it too (core). Reflects to `disabled`, like a native control.

members.name: toolbar
members.description: Static toolbar edge: 'top' (default), 'bottom', 'start', or 'end' places the command toolbar flush against that side of the editor; 'none' hides it. The selection toolbar and context menu are always available while editing (independent of this).

members.name: statusbar
members.description: Status bar edge: 'none' (default), 'top', 'bottom', or 'both'. A dedicated strip of live indicators (word/char count, plus any plugin status items), hugging the editor body — separate from the toolbar zones and shown in read-only too. With 'both', items split across the two strips by their `bar` ('top'/'bottom', default 'bottom').

members.name: theme
members.description: Forced colour scheme: 'dark' swaps the token set (`:host([theme='dark'])`); 'light' (or unset) is the default look. Reflected to the host attribute.

members.name: anchor
members.description: For `view-mode="inline"` only: a CSS selector for the live-page element the floating editor card anchors to (tracked via the core positioning primitive). Absent → the inline card renders in normal flow.

members.name: labels
members.description: Every UI string (rulebook D-NC-24), a PARTIAL object over built-in English, `{name}` placeholders; an empty string = deliberately empty. `placeholder` (default empty = off) is shown while the document is empty. Command items: the camel-cased command id is the item text (`insertLink`, `bold`, `imageBrowserPick`), `<key>Tooltip` its tooltip; toolbar groups `<groupId>Group` (`formatGroup`, …); status `words` / `chars` (`{count}`); prompts `linkUrlPrompt`, `imageUrlPrompt`, `imageAltPrompt`, `codeLanguagePrompt` / `codeLanguageChangePrompt` (`{languages}`); cloud image `cloudImage`, `cloudImageTooltip`, `insertCloudImage`, `cloudImagePickerTitle`, `cloudImagePickerMessage`. Property (object) or JSON attribute (`labels='{"bold":"Tučně"}'`). Applies live (no rebuild).

members.name: beforeActionCallback
members.description: Property only. `(detail) => false | void` (may be async) — runs first on every toolbar / selection-toolbar / context-menu activation, with the `action` event detail. Return `false` to cancel: no `onClick`, no `action` event, no command. Keyboard shortcuts do not pass through it.

members.name: renderLoadingCallback
members.description: Property only. Draws the pending loader (shown while a deferred pipeline's work — e.g. a cloud-image upload — outlives its loader threshold; not while a dialog waits for the user) instead of the default spinner: `({ component, context, containerElement, element, label }) => void | cleanup`, `context` = `'pipeline'`. Fill `containerElement` (it already has `role="status"` + `aria-label` = label `loading`); a returned function runs when the loader is removed. Beats the page-wide `window.components.renderLoadingCallback` (core SPEC §12.14). Read each time the loader shows.

members.name: interactionHost
members.description: Property only. The modal bridge interactive pipeline stages call: `{ request(ctx) }`, `ctx` = the request (`kind`, `title`, `message`, `payload`) + `signal` + `controller` / `element`. Default: a `window.confirm`-backed host. Survives engine rebuilds (e.g. a `plugins` reassignment).

members.name: customStyles
members.description: CSS injected into the editor's shadow root (a `<style class="we-custom-styles">` after the page-wide `window.components['km-editor'].customStyles` layer, so it overrides it). An `@import`ed font is also linked once in the document `<head>` (core). Raw CSS — never put untrusted input here.

members.name: getCustomStylesCallback
members.description: Property only. `(ctx) => string | null` — computes the instance CSS (wins over `customStyles`); `ctx` = `controller` / `element`. Called on every build and whenever `customStyles` / `getCustomStylesCallback` change.

members.name: shouldDefer
members.description: Hold the first build (core, SPEC §6.3): while set when the element first connects, nothing is built and every input, callback and listener assigned meanwhile accumulates; `release()` (or removing the attribute) then builds once. Latched after the first build.

members.name: themeSource
members.description: Where this element reads its theme from instead of the page (core, SPEC §12.10): a CSS selector (nearest matching ancestor, else the first match), `'closest'` (the nearest ancestor carrying a theme signal), or (property only) an `Element`. Unset = the page.

members.name: motion
members.description: Motion level (core, SPEC §12.16): `auto` (default — inherit: the nearest `data-motion` ancestor (a section), else the page level `window.components.motion` / `<html data-motion>`; closest wins), `none` (no transitions, instant scrolling), `snappy` (short) or `smooth` (longer). Sets the shared `--base-duration-*` / `--base-scroll-behavior` tokens on the element through `data-motion`; the OS reduced-motion setting always wins.

members.name: responsive
members.description: Instance responsive rules (core, SPEC §6.7): partial configs on two axes — `device` (keyed by device class `mobile` / `tablet` / `desktop`; a mouse device is `desktop` at any width) and `breakpoint` (keyed by the window-width bucket); the breakpoint entry applies first, the device entry over it (device wins). An object or a JSON attribute, e.g. `{"device":{"tablet":{"presentation":"modal"}},"breakpoint":{"mobile":{…}}}`. Beats page rules (`window.components.responsive*`) and values set on the element; never reflects. An entry of `null` ignores the page rules while it matches.

members.name: responsiveCallback
members.description: Instance computed responsive rule (core, SPEC §6.7): `(ctx) => partial config | null | undefined`, ctx `{ env, deviceClass, breakpoint, element, component, config }` (`config` = base). Runs after `responsive` (wins key by key); re-runs on environment flips, throttled viewport-width changes, rule and config changes. `null` ignores every page rule.

members.name: isReady
members.description: The first build is live (core, SPEC §6.3) — the `ready` event has fired.

members.name: whenReady
members.description: Resolves once the first build is live (also settles when the element is destroyed first). Never rejects.

members.name: release
members.description: Build an element held by `defer` (SPEC §6.3), with everything assigned meanwhile.

members.name: setAttributes
members.description: Apply many inputs (by configKey or attribute name) as ONE rebuild / update. Returns the values it refused (each also fires `input-rejected`).

members.name: batch
members.description: Run `fn` and coalesce every input change it makes into one rebuild / update.

members.name: flush
members.description: Apply pending input writes synchronously, now (SPEC §12.7).

members.name: whenSettled
members.description: Resolves once every staged input change has been applied (SPEC §12.7).

members.name: destroy
members.description: Final teardown (SPEC §6.5): the element is inert afterwards; idempotent.

members.name: isDestroyed
members.description: `destroy()` ran.

members.name: enableLogging
members.description: Set this element's own log level (default `debug`): it logs that level and above, whatever its component type or the page is set to.

members.name: disableLogging
members.description: Silence this element (its own level = `silent`).

members.name: resetLogging
members.description: Clear this element's own log level: it follows its component type / the page again.

members.name: form
members.description: The owning form (form-associated components).

members.name: validity
members.description: Form validity (SPEC §6.6).

members.name: validationMessage
members.description: Form validation message (SPEC §6.6).

members.name: willValidate
members.description: Whether the element takes part in form validation.

members.name: checkValidity
members.description: Form validity check (SPEC §6.6).

members.name: reportValidity
members.description: Form validity check that reports to the user (SPEC §6.6).

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: Initial / default content, interpreted per `contentFormat` (like a native input’s `value` attribute ↔ `defaultValue`). Changing it replaces the document. The live content is the `value` PROPERTY.

attributes.name: content-format
attributes.description: The format of the one document — the lens for content I/O (the `value` attribute and property, the `change` event): 'markdown' (default), 'html', or 'json'. Switching it re-reports the SAME document in the new format — it never rebuilds the document, and (like any assignment) fires no `change`.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Form field name. When set, a light-DOM `<input type="hidden" name="…">` child of the host carries the live content (serialized in `contentFormat`) and submits with the surrounding `<form>`; it is disabled (not submitted) while the editor is disabled, including by a `<fieldset disabled>`. A form reset restores `defaultValue` (attribute `value`) silently — no `change`, like a native `form.reset()`.

attributes.name: view-mode
attributes.description: Presentation: 'edit' (default), 'split' (editor + live output), 'preview' (read-only render), or 'inline' (overlay chrome on a live-page element). `preview` forces read-only. Full layouts arrive in Phase 3; for now the view mode is stored and reflected. Assigning it (property or attribute) is silent — no `view-mode-change`; `setViewMode()` and the view-mode toolbar items fire it.

attributes.name: readonly
attributes.description: Read-only: the content can’t change (no typing, toolbar hidden), but it stays focusable, selectable and copyable. `view-mode="preview"` also forces this on. Reflects to `readonly`.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Disabled: no interaction at all — not editable, not focusable or selectable (the surface is `inert`), toolbar hidden. An ancestor `<fieldset disabled>` disables it too (core). Reflects to `disabled`, like a native control.

attributes.name: toolbar
attributes.description: Static toolbar edge: 'top' (default), 'bottom', 'start', or 'end' places the command toolbar flush against that side of the editor; 'none' hides it. The selection toolbar and context menu are always available while editing (independent of this).

attributes.name: statusbar
attributes.description: Status bar edge: 'none' (default), 'top', 'bottom', or 'both'. A dedicated strip of live indicators (word/char count, plus any plugin status items), hugging the editor body — separate from the toolbar zones and shown in read-only too. With 'both', items split across the two strips by their `bar` ('top'/'bottom', default 'bottom').

attributes.name: theme
attributes.description: Forced colour scheme: 'dark' swaps the token set (`:host([theme='dark'])`); 'light' (or unset) is the default look. Reflected to the host attribute.

attributes.name: anchor
attributes.description: For `view-mode="inline"` only: a CSS selector for the live-page element the floating editor card anchors to (tracked via the core positioning primitive). Absent → the inline card renders in normal flow.

attributes.name: labels
attributes.description: Every UI string (rulebook D-NC-24), a PARTIAL object over built-in English, `{name}` placeholders; an empty string = deliberately empty. `placeholder` (default empty = off) is shown while the document is empty. Command items: the camel-cased command id is the item text (`insertLink`, `bold`, `imageBrowserPick`), `<key>Tooltip` its tooltip; toolbar groups `<groupId>Group` (`formatGroup`, …); status `words` / `chars` (`{count}`); prompts `linkUrlPrompt`, `imageUrlPrompt`, `imageAltPrompt`, `codeLanguagePrompt` / `codeLanguageChangePrompt` (`{languages}`); cloud image `cloudImage`, `cloudImageTooltip`, `insertCloudImage`, `cloudImagePickerTitle`, `cloudImagePickerMessage`. Property (object) or JSON attribute (`labels='{"bold":"Tučně"}'`). Applies live (no rebuild).

attributes.name: custom-styles
attributes.description: CSS injected into the editor's shadow root (a `<style class="we-custom-styles">` after the page-wide `window.components['km-editor'].customStyles` layer, so it overrides it). An `@import`ed font is also linked once in the document `<head>` (core). Raw CSS — never put untrusted input here.

attributes.name: defer
attributes.description: Hold the first build (core, SPEC §6.3): while set when the element first connects, nothing is built and every input, callback and listener assigned meanwhile accumulates; `release()` (or removing the attribute) then builds once. Latched after the first build.

attributes.name: theme-source
attributes.description: Where this element reads its theme from instead of the page (core, SPEC §12.10): a CSS selector (nearest matching ancestor, else the first match), `'closest'` (the nearest ancestor carrying a theme signal), or (property only) an `Element`. Unset = the page.

attributes.name: motion
attributes.description: Motion level (core, SPEC §12.16): `auto` (default — inherit: the nearest `data-motion` ancestor (a section), else the page level `window.components.motion` / `<html data-motion>`; closest wins), `none` (no transitions, instant scrolling), `snappy` (short) or `smooth` (longer). Sets the shared `--base-duration-*` / `--base-scroll-behavior` tokens on the element through `data-motion`; the OS reduced-motion setting always wins.

attributes.name: responsive
attributes.description: Instance responsive rules (core, SPEC §6.7): partial configs on two axes — `device` (keyed by device class `mobile` / `tablet` / `desktop`; a mouse device is `desktop` at any width) and `breakpoint` (keyed by the window-width bucket); the breakpoint entry applies first, the device entry over it (device wins). An object or a JSON attribute, e.g. `{"device":{"tablet":{"presentation":"modal"}},"breakpoint":{"mobile":{…}}}`. Beats page rules (`window.components.responsive*`) and values set on the element; never reflects. An entry of `null` ignores the page rules while it matches.

events.name: change
events.description: The document changed by the user (typing, toolbar, paste, …), a plugin, or `setValue()` (not `{ isSilent: true }`). Assigning `value` / `contentFormat` is silent, like a native `input.value`, and so is a form reset (like a native `form.reset()`). `detail`: `{ value, contentFormat }` — the content serialized in the active `contentFormat`. Twin: `onChange(detail)`.

events.name: ready
events.description: The editor was built and is live for the first time (once per element lifetime; core `BlissElement`). Fires right after the first build — during upgrade for a normal element, or when the `defer` gate is released (`el.release()` / removing `defer`). The host then has the `ready` attribute and matches `:state(ready)`; `el.whenReady()` resolves. `detail`: `controller` / `element`. Twin: `onReady(detail)`.

events.name: view-mode-change
events.description: The view mode was switched by anything but the app's own assignment: a view-mode toolbar item (`source: 'user'`), `setViewMode()` on the element or `controller` (`'api'`, unless `{ isSilent: true }`), or a plugin / pipeline stage through its `setViewMode` port (`'plugin'`). Assigning `viewMode` (attribute `view-mode`) is silent. `detail`: `{ viewMode, oldViewMode, source }`. Twin: `onViewModeChange(detail)`.

events.name: lock-change
events.description: A gating pipeline (e.g. the cloud-image `image:browser:pick`) locked the editor for its run, or released it. `detail`: `{ isLocked }`. Twin: `onLockChange(detail)`.

events.name: value-format-error
events.description: A `getValueFormatCallback` threw while formatting the submitted value. The hidden input then carries an empty string and the host is invalid (`customError`, message = label `valueFormatError`), so the form refuses to submit (`<form novalidate>` submits an empty string); the next successful format clears it. `detail`: `{ error, value }` (`value` = the unformatted document in `contentFormat`). Twin: `onValueFormatError(detail)`.

events.name: action
events.description: A toolbar / selection-toolbar / context-menu item was activated. `detail`: `action` (the command name, or `custom`), `id`, `item`, `source` (`toolbar` | `selection-toolbar` | `context-menu`), `sourceEvent`, `triggerElement`, `dataset`, `state` (the ProseMirror state). Fires after the item’s `onClick` and the command (a notification after the fact; `state` is the snapshot from activation); `beforeActionCallback` → `false` cancels. Keyboard shortcuts do not fire it. Twin: `onAction(detail)`.

events.name: input-rejected
events.description: Fired when a written value is refused (core, SPEC §6): an invalid attribute or property value, or an unknown `setAttributes()` key. The element warns and keeps its previous value. Detail `{ configKey, attribute?, value, reason?, kept, source }`. Twin callback `onInputRejected`.
